title: Short Stuff: Colorful Noises
summary: Short Stuff episode on colored noises: brown, white, and pink noise (plus purple and blue noise mentioned). The hosts cover the origin of "brown noise" in Robert Brown's observation of pollen movement and the later mathematical sound generation, the nature sounds each resembles (rapids, rain, thunder, breeze), a bamboo-wind sound in a Kyoto park, and pink noise as a middle ground. They discuss sleep studies (Oxford 2017 white noise, a pink noise vocabulary study, a Northwestern 2017 study of older adults, an Iranian hospital study of coronary patients), and offer practical tips such as using a speaker for more bass and a pillow-and-phone trick. They mention the Dwell Spring sound app, created by Brandon Reid.

segments.title: Opening welcome
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Short Stuff episode on color noises.

segments.title: Brown noise and personal use
segments.summary: Hosts discuss listening to brown noise for relaxation, focus, and sleep, and describe how it sounds like rapids, heavy rain, or distant thunder.

segments.title: Origin of brown noise and Robert Brown
segments.summary: Josh explains the name comes not from the color but from Robert Brown's early 1800s observation of pollen moving in water, later explained by Einstein, and Speaker 2 notes that the mathematical formula for those random movements was used to generate the sound.

segments.title: Transition to white noise
segments.summary: The hosts move on to white noise, described as a high-frequency sound resembling light rain or a gentle breeze, used for masking and with noise-canceling headphones.

segments.title: Bamboo wind sound and video game anecdote
segments.summary: Josh mentions a Kyoto bamboo park where the sound of wind through bamboo is protected as a heritage site. Speaker 2 recalls wind sounds in a video game, and Josh corrects the reference.

segments.title: Pink noise explained
segments.summary: Josh describes pink noise as a compromise between white and brown noise, with some mid-range and moderate emphasis on low and high frequencies.

segments.title: Listening to noise samples and the Dwell Spring app
segments.summary: Speaker 2 plays samples of pink, white, and brown noise from an app. The hosts mention purple and blue noise and praise the Dwell Spring app by Brandon Reid, which includes a box fan, airplane cabin, and fireplace-in-thunderstorm sounds.

segments.title: Sleep studies on noise
segments.summary: The hosts review studies: Oxford 2017 found people fell asleep 40 percent faster with white noise; a study of 16 young adults found pink noise improved vocabulary recall, with the word pickle cited; a 2017 Northwestern study of 13 older adults found pink noise gave deeper sleep and better recall.

segments.title: Iranian hospital study and hospital sleep
segments.summary: Josh describes a study in Iran of 60 elderly coronary patients where the white noise group's sleep quality stayed steady during hospital stays while the control group's degraded. The hosts vent about hospital noise and disruptions.

segments.title: Tips for using sound machines
segments.summary: Speaker 2 suggests trying different noises and volumes, and says playing sound through a speaker gives more bass than a phone. They also describe a napping trick of placing the phone under a pillow to trap the sound.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up the episode and the show gets a closing credit as an iHeartRadio production.
